C-SUPERSEDE-RECORD.Summary: Make ngrace supersede fold any open epoch before it archives, so the discarded bundle keeps its run record, and document that the verb discards governance, never code. Range-close with a new discarded kind, not by emitting terminal. The kind is unreachable except through that abandon: advanceCursor refuses it, and one purpose-named export is the only production writer. No new src file.
C-SUPERSEDE-RECORD.Problem:
ngrace supersede writes superseded, names the replacement, and renames the bundle into archive/. It does not fold. Measured 2026-09-01 on this tree:
C-SUPERSEDE-VERB (five tasks executed): archive has run-ledger.xml with 3 approve Decisions, 0 Epoch elements, 0 attempts; run/ is absent; status epochCount=0. C-LINT-PHASE-HONESTY (five tasks, same class of event): Epoch-1, 10 attempts (4 fail, 6 pass), 4 named signatures; run/ present and empty after fold; epochCount=1. The only difference is that the second had cursor advance --kind terminal and cursor fold run by hand first. src/grace-supersede.ts contains no reference to fold, Epoch, or run/.
Probe of HEAD (temp project, writeMinimalNgraceProject): open an epoch with no terminal, then supersede. Exit 0. Archive holds run/1-T-001-opened.xml and no run-ledger.xml. Rename preserves loose files; it does not write an Epoch. The measuring instrument (status.epochCount, ledger attempts) therefore prices the discard at zero. That is F128 / F134.1 / F134.2.
Fold does not no-op on a never-executed bundle. cursor fold --change C-PHASE-RULE-PIN prints "No loose run/ events to fold for C-PHASE-RULE-PIN." and exits 1 (stderr; stdout empty). The same refuse hits C-SUPERSEDE-VERB (ledger with Decisions, 0 Epochs, no loose events). Calling foldEpoch unconditionally from supersede would refuse the C-PHASE-RULE-PIN shape.
Fold's unterminated-range check is not silent. Probe: opened event, no terminal, cursor fold exits 1, stderr "unterminated range for w0", no ledger written, loose files remain. Grammar also requires a terminal inside every live allocation (src/artifact/grammar.ts:1119-1127 ledger.range-unterminated). So a discarded open epoch cannot fold unless a range-closing event sits in range.
The draft of this spec closed that range by auto-emitting kind=terminal from the verb. That is a lie: terminal is a completion judgment, and skills/ngrace/ngrace-execute/SKILL.md:87 forbids the binary from deriving one — "recover --fix does **not** emit terminal." D21 (2026-09-01) ruled that if an operation cannot be represented truthfully under the current schema without breaking that rule, the constraint is wrong, not the rule. The schema therefore gains a discarded kind meaning abandoned, and supersede emits that kind, not terminal.
A later draft of this spec left cursor advance --kind discarded legal on the same write path as other known kinds, with the skill forbidding its misuse. That makes the restriction advisory. Advisory rules here do not hold: the MustPassCommand prohibition sat in skill prose while 21 archived plans broke it, which is why C-PHASE-RULE-PIN exists. A general kind parameter that accepts discarded from any caller — CLI or library — is the same advisory rule one layer down. discarded must be unreachable except through an abandon.
This is not a reversal of F134.2. F134.2 rejected a new kind as a legibility fix and was correct: measured on archived C-LINT-PHASE-HONESTY, cursor show reports State: complete (cursor lifecycle) and Complete: n/a (work-completion); status reports specStatus=superseded, planStatus=superseded, epochCount=1, derivedStates=[]. No surface claims the abandoned work completed. The kind returns on a different and stronger ground: the binary cannot produce the folded record at all without asserting a completion that did not happen.
Nothing in the verb description, README CLI row, or skills states that supersede discards governance and never code. F127's recorded close is the precedent: T-001-T-007 complete, in scope, and green; nothing needs reverting. The replacement carries implementation forward. A reader may assume the opposite; that difference is the whole cost model.
RM-PILOT-APPROVAL review.md:80 calls an amendment count in the ledger "the measuring instrument". An archive that prices discarded executions at zero cannot support that decision. This bundle is the first of the three instrument bundles F134.1 named (discard, then amendment counter, then effort). The latter two stay out.

Goals.Goal: supersedeChangeBundle folds any open epoch into run-ledger.xml before the status write and rename, so an abandoned execution archives with its Epoch, attempts, and signatures intact without the operator running a range-closer and fold by hand.
When that fold needs a range-closer, the verb emits kind=discarded, never kind=terminal. discarded means the epoch was abandoned. terminal keeps its meaning: the operator judged the work finished.

discarded is unreachable except through that abandon. advanceCursor refuses kind=discarded. The CLI inherits the refusal because it forwards --kind to advanceCursor. One purpose-named export in src/grace-cursor.ts writes the event through the module-private writer and folds. supersedeChangeBundle is the only production caller.
A bundle that never executed (C-PHASE-RULE-PIN shape: no loose run/ events) still supersedes. Fold is skipped, not invoked.

Document on the verb itself and on the README.md CLI Overview row that supersede discards the governance record, never the code, and that it folds first. Teach the same two facts where agents are told to run the verb (ngrace-plan approved_plan_immutability and ngrace-execute preflight). Teach discarded in ngrace-execute cursor_kinds: the operator never emits this kind; ngrace supersede is the verb that does.

AcceptanceCriteria.AC-FOLD-BEFORE-ARCHIVE: On a throwaway project, open an epoch (advanceCursor openEpoch, no range-closer), run ngrace supersede --change C-OLD --replacement C-NEW. Exit 0. The archived C-OLD has a run-ledger.xml Epoch containing the opened event, a kind=discarded event, no kind=terminal event added by the verb, and no foldable loose events under run/. status for that change reports epochCount greater than 0. HEAD today archives the opened file and no ledger; that probe must go red first, then green.
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-NO-EPOCH-NOOP: supersede of a spec-only active bundle with no run/ directory (C-PHASE-RULE-PIN shape) exits 0 and archives. It must not invoke foldEpoch in a way that surfaces "No loose run/ events to fold" (that CLI currently exits 1). Existing spec-only supersede tests stay green.

That discarded entry states the operator never emits this kind and names ngrace supersede as the verb that does. KNOWN_KIND_STATE maps discarded to CursorState discarded, not to complete. Packaged ngrace-execute stays byte-identical to canonical.
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-DISCARDED-REFUSE: Both directions on one throwaway shape: open an epoch with advanceCursor openEpoch, no range-closer, replacement bundle present. (1) Refuse: advanceCursor with kind: "discarded" throws GraceCommandError whose code is invalid-arguments and whose message is exactly kind "discarded" is reserved; ngrace supersede writes it when abandoning an open epoch. The refuse writes no new run/ file. ngrace cursor advance --change C-OLD --task T-001 --kind discarded on that same tree exits nonzero; stderr is that same message; no discarded-specific branch exists in the CLI advance defineCommand block (it still forwards --kind). (2) Permit: ngrace supersede --change C-OLD --replacement C-NEW on that same shape exits 0; the archived run-ledger.xml Epoch contains a discarded event and no verb-emitted terminal. A refuse never contrasted with this permit is not a discrimination.
